questions.q: What does the closed form of the forward process let you do during training?
options: Jump to any noise level in one step without simulating the chain
questions.answer: Jump to any noise level in one step without simulating the chain
questions.why: x_t = √ᾱ_t x_0 + √(1−ᾱ_t) ε samples any level directly. The lab confirms it matches the 1000-step chain.

questions.q: In L_simple, what is the training target?
options: The noise ε that was added
questions.answer: The noise ε that was added
questions.why: Ho et al. 2020 eq. 14 regresses ε_θ on the ε used to make x_t.

questions.q: For SD 1.x, what does sigma_max = 14.61 mean?
options: At the last step the sample equals x_0 plus noise of standard deviation 14.61, in the rescaled picture
The latent values are clipped at 14.61
questions.answer: At the last step the sample equals x_0 plus noise of standard deviation 14.61, in the rescaled picture
questions.why: σ = √((1−ᾱ)/ᾱ), the noise level after dividing by √ᾱ_t.

questions.q: Is the final step of the SD 1.x schedule pure noise?
options: No, about 0.068 of the signal survives
questions.answer: No, about 0.068 of the signal survives
questions.why: Lin et al. 2023 give x_T = 0.068265 x_0 + 0.997667 ε, which is SNR 0.0047 and matches the lab.

questions.q: Why is L_simple not simply the "correct" objective?
options: It cannot be computed on a GPU
It drops the weights of the variational bound, and that choice is empirical
questions.answer: It drops the weights of the variational bound, and that choice is empirical
questions.why: Ho et al. describe it as a weighted variational bound. They chose it because samples were better.
